summary: A BBN notice that use of IMP DDT, the debugging facility on the network's IMP machines, would be restricted, after workshop attendees worried that uncontrolled use endangered access control. The Network Control Center still needed to be able to use it at any IMP, so some commands were protected. It was written for security reasons.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC discusses restricting access to the DDT debugging facility on IMPs. It describes safeguards for powerful commands and a planned extension of those controls.

subtitle: A plan to restrict access to the IMP debugging facility.

tldr.problem: Workshop participants raised concerns that uncontrolled use of IMP DDT could make access controls vulnerable to interception or tampering.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes existing safeguards for commands affecting the running IMP program and a planned requirement for enabling actions before any DDT access.
tldr.outcome: The author says the change should discourage unauthorized use but would not stop a determined, malicious attack.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 521's status as Unknown. The RFC documents planned access restrictions and states their security limits.

sections.title: Why DDT Access Was a Concern
sections.content:
At a workshop on automated resource sharing, participants raised concerns that uncontrolled use of IMP DDT could make access-control mechanisms vulnerable to interception or tampering. The RFC also notes that Network Control Center use of DDT was increasing.

DDT remained important for network operations, including diagnostics and loading code, so the issue was how to control access without removing operational use.
sections.plainLanguage: Workshop participants were concerned that unrestricted DDT use could expose or alter access controls. The Network Control Center still needed DDT for network work.

sections.title: Enabling Protected DDT Commands
sections.content:
At the time of the RFC, commands that could affect the running IMP program required sense switch 4 to be on at the site or a software override flag to be enabled. Only the BBN IMP teletype, the BBN TIP teletype, and a PDP-1 could enable the override.

The RFC says the IMP system would soon be modified so that any DDT access required the same enabling actions. The Network Control Center monitored the flags.
sections.plainLanguage: Powerful DDT commands required a local switch or a software override. The RFC announces a planned extension that would require those controls for any DDT access.

sections.title: Operational Use and Limits
sections.content:
The change was intended to preserve the Network Control Center's ability to use DDT at any IMP and to let site personnel operate DDT when asked by the Network Control Center. The RFC did not intend to prohibit occasional DDT messages between sites.

The author says the change should discourage hackers but acknowledges that it would not protect a node from a determined, malicious attack.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators would keep the DDT access they needed, and occasional DDT messages between sites would continue. The author says the safeguards would not stop a determined attack.
